notes.meaning: David cries out to the Lord with great urgency, asking God to come quickly to his aid. He knows that prayer is his surest refuge in times of deep trouble, so he pleads for God to hear his voice. When believers face sudden danger, they can turn directly to God with honest and earnest requests for help.

David asks that his humble prayers be accepted just like the fragrant incense burned daily in the tabernacle. Because he was far from the sanctuary and could not join in public worship, he offered the lifting of his hands in place of the regular evening offering. Sincere prayer and personal devotion are spiritual sacrifices that bring true pleasure to God.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: In Orthodox liturgy, this verse is sung every evening at Vespers while incense is offered, reminding worshippers that their prayers rise acceptably to God through Christ.

notes.meaning: David asks the Lord to place a guard over his mouth, as if his lips were a defended doorway. When provoked by cruel and slanderous enemies, he knows how easy it is to blurt out rash or bitter words. He realizes that his own willpower is not enough, so he asks God for the grace to control his tongue.

David pleads with God to keep his heart from leaning toward anything evil. He does not want to join wicked men in their sinful schemes or enjoy the flattering treats and advantages won through corruption. Knowing how tempting sin can look, he asks God to give him an appetite that turns away from ungodly delights.

David welcomes the honest correction of a godly person, calling it an act of genuine kindness. Even though a rebuke can sting at first, it heals and refreshes the soul like soothing olive oil poured on the head. Instead of holding a grudge, David promises to return the favor by praying for his faithful friends whenever they face hardship.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Following ancient translations like the Greek Septuagint and Latin Vulgate, this verse is read as a request never to let the flattering, soothing oil of wicked people anoint the speaker's head.

notes.meaning: Corrupt and tyrannical leaders will eventually be thrown down from high places and brought to ruin. When those oppressors fall, the everyday people who followed them will finally listen to David's gentle and righteous words. Hard times often open people's ears to value God's truth, which they previously ignored.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars find the Hebrew phrasing here and in verse 7 so difficult and abrupt that they consider the lines to be displaced from another context.

notes.meaning: David describes his group of followers as being pushed to the very edge of death, looking like scattered bones lying unburied at an open grave. They feel shattered, just like wood chips scattered by an axe or dirt torn open by a plow. Yet the image of plowing contains hidden hope, because ground is broken open so that new life can sprout from the soil.

Despite how dark and hopeless his situation looks, David keeps his eyes fixed on the Lord. He takes refuge in God alone and asks that his life not be poured out like wasted water. Keeping our focus on God keeps our faith steady even when everything around us seems lost.

David asks God to protect him from the hidden snares and traps laid by his enemies. Wicked people often work in secret, trying to trip up the righteous with clever tricks and sudden attacks. Because human eyes cannot see every hidden danger, David trusts God's watchful eye to keep his feet safe.

David asks that the wicked get caught in the very nets they wove to trap others, while he passes safely by. God's justice often causes evil plans to rebound on the people who designed them. Believers can leave justice in God's hands, trusting Him to deliver them from the schemes of the ungodly.
